title: Judgment on Moab

questions.question: Concerning what nation is this long prophecy of judgment in chapter 48 directed?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48 (ESV) is titled "Judgment on Moab", beginning with "Concerning Moab. Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel..."

questions.question: "Woe to Nebo, for it is laid waste! Kiriathaim is put to shame, it is taken; the... is put to shame and broken down."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:1 (ESV): "the fortress is put to shame and broken down."

questions.question: "The renown of Moab is no more. In... they planned evil against her: 'Come, let us cut her off from being a nation!'"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:2 (ESV): "In Heshbon they planned evil against her:"

questions.question: "Flee! Save yourselves! You will be like a... in the desert!"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:6 (ESV): "Flee! Save yourselves! You will be like a juniper in the desert!"

questions.question: "For, because you trusted in your... and your... , you also shall be taken;"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:7 (ESV): "For, because you trusted in your works and your treasures, you also shall be taken;"

questions.question: What god of the Moabites will go into exile, with his priests and his officials?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:7 (ESV): "and Chemosh shall go into exile with his priests and his officials."

questions.question: "Cursed is he who does the work of the Lord with slackness, and cursed is he who keeps back his... from bloodshed."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:10 (ESV): "and cursed is he who keeps back his sword from bloodshed."

questions.question: "Moab has been at ease from his... and has settled on his... ; he has not been emptied from vessel to vessel, nor has he gone into exile; so his taste remains in him, and his scent is not changed."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:11 (ESV): "Moab has been at ease from his youth and has settled on his dregs;"

questions.question: "Therefore, behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I shall send to him... who will pour him, and they shall empty his vessels and break his jars in pieces."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:12 (ESV): "I shall send to him pourers who will pour him, and they shall empty his vessels and break his jars in pieces."

questions.question: "How can you say, 'We are heroes and mighty men of... '?"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:14 (ESV): "How can you say, 'We are heroes and mighty men of war'?"

questions.question: What image is used for the destruction of Moab's strength? "The mighty... is broken, the glorious...!"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:17 (ESV): "Say, 'How the mighty scepter is broken, the glorious staff!'"

questions.question: "Come down from your glory, and sit on the parched ground, O inhabitant of... ! For the destroyer of Moab has come up against you; he has destroyed your strongholds."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:18 (ESV): "Come down from your glory, and sit on the parched ground, O inhabitant of Dibon!"

questions.question: "Make him... , because he magnified himself against the Lord, so that Moab shall wallow in his vomit, and he too shall be held in derision."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:26 (ESV): "Make him drunk, because he magnified himself against the Lord,"

questions.question: "Was not... a derision to you? Was he found among thieves, that whenever you spoke of him you wagged your head?"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:27 (ESV): "Was not Israel a derision to you? Was he found among thieves, that whenever you spoke of him you wagged your head?"

questions.question: "Yet I will restore the... of Moab in the latter days, declares the Lord."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:47 (ESV): "Yet I will restore the fortunes of Moab in the latter days, declares the Lord. Thus far is the judgment on Moab."

key_verse_text: "Yet I will restore the fortunes of Moab in the latter days, declares the Lord. Thus far is the judgment on Moab."
